A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAGE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably despite additions, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on LLaVA and Qwen2.5-VL, component and hyperparameter ablations, and defense and detection experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results on another LVLM, additional tasks, attack comparators, transfer, optimizers, runtime and existing defenses.

M1.justification: v2 corrects the specified RDA gradient flow: Section 4.3 changes the stopped-gradient distribution from p(s) to p(d), and Algorithm 1 explicitly detaches the distortion target. The remaining CAGE procedure is retained; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: The original VQA-v2, TextVQA and GQA coverage remains. Appendix E.7 adds generative captioning on COCO, a different task despite COCO already supplying VQA-v2 images; E.11 adds driving-focused DriveQA. These substantially extend task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained VEAttack comparison, v2 evaluates AttackVLM-ii and VT-Attack in Table 13 and an EOT budget-sampling baseline in Table 17. It also adds a Random selection control in Table 3 and RobustCLIP/FARE and DPS defense comparisons in Tables 20–21.

E3.justification: Original main settings remain, while new protocols include InternVL3-8B, 100-sample captioning evaluation with CIDEr, black-box encoder transfer using epsilon 16/255 and 100 PGD steps, APGD/MI-FGSM comparisons, and matched 224-by-224 standard/FARE victims. Section 5.3 also replaces CRA with its complement, CRD.

E4.justification: The original component, perturbation-budget, weighting, scoring and budget-prior ablations remain. New analyses test encoder transfer, budget sampling versus CAGE, optimizer dependence, computational cost, a random-selection defense control, and resilience against existing defenses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional result rows and average runtime measurements do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Table 2 and the retained Qwen, ablation and detection scores are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results. For example, Table 7 reports 39.9% versus 33.4% robust accuracy for baseline versus CAGE on InternVL3/VisionZIP at 72 tokens; Table 14 reports captioning CIDEr of 0.1998 versus 0.1090 at 64 tokens. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 runs.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 revises the defined normalized metric from CRA = R/C to CRD = 1 - R/C, measuring degradation instead of retention. This limited mathematical-definition change adds no theorem or proof; the existing derivations and defense formulas remain.

C1.justification: The central claims about the optimization-inference mismatch, CAGE under unknown compression budgets, and the need for compression-aware evaluation remain. The abstract's replacement of robustness overestimation with incomplete exposure of vulnerabilities restates the same scientific claim.

C2.justification: Appendix E.9 adds a substantive applicability boundary, attributing limited black-box gains to difficulty transferring compression-alignment signals. E.10 interprets the optimizer and budget-sampling controls, while F.1 discusses stronger defenses alongside training and inference costs. The original Appendix G limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link, specifies the transfer surrogate and its PGD settings, documents resolution and encoder controls for RobustCLIP, and reports attack runtime. The original core hyperparameters and RTX 4090 hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature and discussion on robust encoders, DPS, encoder-based transfer and reasoning applications while retaining its original research positioning. VEAttack's updated publication citation refers to the same work, rather than a newly introduced research direction.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. Local edits correct RDA wording, introduce CRD terminology, update correspondence and publication information, and add acknowledgements. Appendix D is reorganized for multiple LVLMs, and E/F gain experiment-specific subsections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the tabular presentation across model, task, attack, transfer, optimizer, runtime and defense comparisons. Table 3 gains Random rows; v1 Table 11 moves into the main text as v2 Table 4; Figure 4 is redrawn for CRD with reversed token-budget ordering. Other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by addressing v1's reliance on one principal attack baseline and VQA tasks, testing alternative budget handling and optimizers, and documenting limited black-box transfer. Runtime and existing-defense comparisons improve practical assessment, while the RDA correction resolves an implementation ambiguity. Some added protocols remain underspecified and uncertainty estimates are absent, but the gains in evidential support and applicability assessment are substantial.
